mainTopic: Permitted טומאה, the הואיל challenge about other offerings slaughtered as a פסח, רבי שמלאי and ספר יוחסין, and intent about the people who will eat the פסח.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion of which kind of טומאה a ברייתא called 'permitted from its general rule.' The גמרא gives two answers. The first is that it means impure people, which is allowed when the ציבור is impure. The second is that it means impure meat, which is allowed in the case of a פסח brought in טומאה. Next, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע uses a ברייתא about a פסח שעברה שנתו to challenge strict הואיל reasoning. רב פפא answers from the verse 'זבח פסח הוא': the two rules about a פסח and other offerings are tied together. The גמרא then tells how רבי שמלאי asked רבי יוחנן to teach him ספר יוחסין. רבי יוחנן was reluctant, but he answered רבי שמלאי's question about why mixed לשמו ושלא לשמו intent disqualifies a פסח while mixed לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו intent does not. He gives four differences, and רב אשי shows that two of them are really one. After some praise of the lost ספר יוחסין, the amud ends with אחרים's ruling on intent for מולים and ערלים, along with a challenge that is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Impurity of the meat is never permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the ברייתא cannot mean impurity of the meat, because impure sacrificial meat is never allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the ברייתא means impurity of the meat, where was that ever permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is testing one possible reading of 'טומאה that was permitted' and rejecting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא described טומאה as something that 'was permitted from its general rule.' The גמרא first checks whether this could mean טומאת בשר (impure sacrificial meat). It rejects that reading, because there seems to be no case where eating impure קדשים is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the sacrificial meat itself
Where?
It was permitted

phrases.english: About impurity of the meat: where was it permitted?
phrases.notes: This amud starts mid-sentence. Just before it, the גמרא offers this as a first suggestion: 'if you say it means impurity of the meat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּטוּמְאַת בָּשָׂר — הֵיכָא הוּתְּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the clarification, begun on the previous amud, of which טומאה the ברייתא meant.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'טומאה that was permitted' as טומאת בשר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Impure sacrificial meat is never permitted, so the phrase 'was permitted' would not fit it.

steps.title: It means impurity of people, permitted in the community
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must mean impurity of people, which is permitted when the ציבור as a whole is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it means impurity of people. And where was that permitted from its general rule? In the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the 'permitted טומאה' is impurity of people, which is allowed for a ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An impure person normally may not bring or eat a קרבן. However, when most of the ציבור is impure, the קרבן is brought anyway in טומאה. That is the case where this rule is 'permitted from its general rule.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Impurity of the people (the owners or offerers)
Was permitted out of its general rule; has a built-in exception
The community (here, when most of the community is impure)

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle that טומאה הותרה בציבור (impurity is permitted for the community) is a basic rule for קרבנות ציבור and for קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: about impurity of the people,
and where was it permitted from its rule? In the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having rejected impurity of the meat, the גמרא settles on impurity of people.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which טומאה did the ברייתא mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טומאת גברי (impurity of people), which is permitted for a ציבור.

steps.title: The two clauses would discuss different impurities
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this reading makes the ברייתא inconsistent: its first part is about impure meat and its second part is about impure people.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the first clause is about impurity of the meat, and the latter clause is about impurity of people?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given, because it makes the ברייתא switch topics in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the ברייתא spoke about impurity of the meat. If the 'permitted' part means impurity of people, the argument compares two different things. Normally an argument should compare the same kind of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause
The latter clause

phrases.english: The first clause is about impurity of the meat,
the latter clause is about impurity of the people?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא בְּטוּמְאַת בָּשָׂר, סֵיפָא בְּטוּמְאַת גַּבְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'permitted טומאה' means impurity of people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It splits the ברייתא into two different kinds of טומאה, which seems like an unfair comparison.

steps.title: The argument uses the general name of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the switch. The ברייתא argues from the general category of טומאה, not one specific kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. He is arguing from the general name 'impurity.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the switch is acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's point is that the category called 'טומאה' has places where it is permitted. It does not matter whether the permission comes from impurity of meat or impurity of people. Both share the name טומאה, and that shared name is enough for the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
The general name or category of impurity
He is challenging; he is arguing from

phrases.english: Yes. He argues from the general name of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין — שֵׁם טוּמְאָה קָפָרֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise and explains why it is not a problem.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each clause must discuss the exact same type of טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument works from the broad category 'טומאה,' so mixing the two types is fine.

steps.title: Second answer: impure meat is permitted for the פסח
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the whole ברייתא is about impurity of the meat. Impure meat is permitted when a פסח is brought in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you wish, say: the whole ברייתא is about impurity of the meat. Where was it permitted? With impurity of the פסח, as we learned in a משנה: A פסח that comes in טומאה is eaten in טומאה, because from the start it only came to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer that keeps the ברייתא consistent. It finds a case where impure meat really is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 assumed that impure meat is never allowed, but this answer shows an exception. When a פסח is brought in טומאה because the ציבור is impure, its meat may be eaten in טומאה. This is because the whole purpose of a פסח is eating, so the ברייתא can stay about impurity of the meat from start to finish.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
All of it; the entire ברייתא
A פסח offered in a state of impurity
For the purpose of eating

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every קרבן brought in טומאה may be eaten. For other קרבנות ציבור brought in טומאה, the blood is sprinkled but the meat is not eaten. Only the פסח is eaten in טומאה, because eating is its whole purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain 'טומאה that was permitted.' (1) It means impurity of people, permitted for a ציבור, and the ברייתא argues from the general name 'טומאה.' (2) It means impurity of the meat, permitted for a פסח הבא בטומאה.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: all of it is about impurity of the meat,
and where was it permitted? With impurity of the Paschal offering,
as we learned: a Paschal offering that comes in impurity
is eaten in impurity,
because from its outset it came only to be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כּוּלַּהּ בְּטוּמְאַת בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא of step 3 and overturns the assumption of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the source and brings a supporting משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Impure sacrificial meat is never permitted (step 1).
steps.terutzMaskana: Impure meat is permitted for a פסח brought in טומאה, so the whole ברייתא can discuss impurity of the meat.

steps.title: רב הונא brings a ברייתא about a פסח past its first year
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע begins an objection. He quotes a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר disqualifies, and רבי יהושע validates, an offering slaughtered on ערב פסח as a פסח when it cannot really be one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objected: A פסח that has passed its first year, and he slaughtered it at its proper time as a פסח, and likewise one who slaughters other offerings as a פסח at its proper time: רבי אליעזר disqualifies, and רבי יהושע validates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new objection by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the source. The actual point of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח must be in its first year, so once it is older it automatically becomes a שלמים. Slaughtering it, or another שלמים, 'as a פסח' on ערב פסח is a case of a different קרבן brought under the name פסח. רבי אליעזר disqualifies it, while רבי יהושע holds it is valid, as a שלמים brought with the wrong intent.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסח animal that has passed its first year (and so cannot be a פסח)
At its proper time (Erev Pesach afternoon)
For its own purpose (as a פסח)
Disqualifies
Validates

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse רבי יהושע in the ברייתא with רב יהושע, the father of רב הונא who raises the objection. They are different people.

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua objected:
A Paschal offering that passed its year,
and he slaughtered it at its time for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֲחֵרִים לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח בִּזְמַנּוֹ —
phrases.english: and likewise one who slaughters other offerings as a Paschal offering at its time:
Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies,
and Rabbi Yehoshua validates.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new objection after the טומאה discussion is resolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view (associated with רב חסדא) that we apply הואיל reasoning to be strict.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits רבי אליעזר's disqualification to בזמנו. The next step infers that שלא בזמנו the offering is valid, which contradicts strict הואיל reasoning.

steps.title: Why not disqualify outside its time too?
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, the גמרא learns that רבי אליעזר disqualifies only at the פסח's proper time. It then asks why the "since" (הואיל) reasoning does not make it disqualified at other times as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it is disqualified is that it happened at its proper time. This implies that at another time, it is valid. But why? Let us say: since it disqualifies at its proper time, it should also disqualify when it is not at its proper time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the objection that began in step 6. It draws a careful inference from the ברייתא, then challenges that inference with "since" (הואיל) reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions ערב פסח, so we learn that during the rest of the year, another offering slaughtered as a פסח stays valid. But the earlier approach (associated with רב חסדא) uses הואיל to be strict: if something is disqualified in one setting, it should be disqualified everywhere. If הואיל works, the offering should be disqualified all year, and that clashes with what the ברייתא implies.

keyTerms.meaning: At its proper time; here, ערב פסח, when the פסח is brought
Not at its proper time; any other time of year
"Since": reasoning that because a rule applies in one case, it should apply in a related case
Disqualifies (an offering)
"But why?": opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The inference "הא שלא בזמנו כשר" is not the problem. It is the accepted reading of the ברייתא. The problem is that הואיל reasoning seems to contradict it.

phrases.english: The reason is that it was at its proper time,
phrases.notes: On ערב פסח, the time of the פסח

phrases.english: which implies that not at its proper time, it is valid.
But why? Let us say:
since it disqualifies at its proper time,
it should also disqualify not at its proper time!
phrases.notes: Here comes the challenge, based on הואיל ('since') reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? נֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וּבִזְמַנּוֹ פּוֹסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע began in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of הואיל reasoning to be strict
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If הואיל applies, then disqualification at the proper time should carry over to other times. Yet the ברייתא implies that outside its time the offering is valid.

steps.title: רב פפא: the word "הוא" creates a special rule
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the פסח is different because of the verse "זבח פסח הוא." The word "הוא" teaches that the פסח must stay as it is. A פסח may not be brought for other offerings, and other offerings may not be brought as a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is different there, because the verse says, "And you shall say: it is a פסח offering." "It" means as it is: it may not be brought for the sake of others, and others may not be brought for its sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by showing that the rule here comes from a verse, not from הואיל reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "הוא" ("it") teaches that a פסח must keep its own identity. That gives two rules: a פסח slaughtered for another offering is a problem, and another offering slaughtered as a פסח is a problem. Because one verse produces both rules, they are tied together.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is different there": shows why a case does not follow the general rule
"It is a פסח offering" (שמות יב:כז)
As it is; in its original, unchanged state
For the sake of other offerings
For its sake; here, as a פסח

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is different there,
because the verse says:
"And you shall say: It is a Pesach offering"
"it" means as it is:
not it for the sake of other offerings,
and not other offerings for its sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הואיל challenge of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case by pointing to a special verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The disqualification is based on general logic, so הואיל should spread it to all times
steps.terutzMaskana: The disqualification comes from the word "הוא," which pairs two rules together

steps.title: The two rules mirror each other
steps.stepSummary: Because the two rules are linked, they follow each other. At its time, a פסח for others is disqualified, so others as a פסח are disqualified. Outside its time, a פסח for others is valid, so others as a פסח are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: At its proper time, when a פסח is disqualified if brought for others, other offerings are disqualified if brought for its sake. Not at its proper time, when a פסח is valid if brought for others, other offerings are valid if brought for its sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies רב פפא's verse to show exactly why other offerings stay valid outside the פסח's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules from "הוא" are mirrors of each other. During the rest of the year, a פסח slaughtered for another purpose is valid, so the mirror rule must also allow other offerings slaughtered as a פסח. The result comes from the verse's pairing, so הואיל reasoning does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: Through the word "הוא," the two rules (a פסח for others, and others as a פסח) are tied together. Wherever one applies, so does the other. Outside its time, both are valid, so הואיל reasoning does not apply.

phrases.english: At its proper time, when it is disqualified for the sake of others,
other offerings are disqualified for its sake.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא כָּשֵׁר לְשׁוּם אֲחֵרִים —
phrases.english: Not at its proper time, when it is valid for the sake of others,
other offerings are valid for its sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַנּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא פָּסוּל לְשׁוּם אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב פפא's verse to show its result
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Other offerings slaughtered as a פסח are valid outside its time because their rule mirrors the rule for a פסח slaughtered for other purposes, so הואיל reasoning is not needed.

steps.title: רבי שמלאי asks רבי יוחנן to teach him
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. רבי שמלאי asks רבי יוחנן to teach him ספר יוחסין. רבי יוחנן asks where he is from (לוד) and where he lives now (נהרדעא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי came before רבי יוחנן. He said to him: Will the master teach me ספר יוחסין? He said to him: Where are you from? He answered: From לוד. And where do you live? In נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to a story. רבי יוחנן's questions here set up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ספר יוחסין was a body of teachings on דברי הימים. רבי יוחנן asks about רבי שמלאי's background because, as the next step shows, he has a policy about whom he teaches this material to.

keyTerms.meaning: The Book of Genealogies: teachings on דברי הימים
Will the master teach me
Your place of residence
A city in ארץ ישראל
A city in בבל

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Simlai came before Rabbi Yochanan.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נִיתְנֵי לִי מָר סֵפֶר יוּחֲסִין.
phrases.english: He said to him: Will the master teach me the Book of Genealogies?
He said to him: Where are you from?
He said to him: From Lod.
And where do you live? In Neharde'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story after the halachic discussion has ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמלאי asks to learn ספר יוחסין, and רבי יוחנן asks about his origin and residence

steps.title: רבי יוחנן refuses but gives in
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that this material is not taught to people from לוד or from נהרדעא, and certainly not to someone connected to both. רבי שמלאי presses him until he agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We do not teach it to people of לוד or to people of נהרדעא, and certainly not to you, who are from לוד and live in נהרדעא. He pressed him, and he agreed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a reason for refusing. רבי שמלאי keeps asking until רבי יוחנן finally agrees to teach him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One explanation is that people from these places had a reputation for being haughty and weak in Torah learning, so they were not taught this material. רבי שמלאי has a double connection: he is from לוד and lives in נהרדעא. Even so, his persistence wins רבי יוחנן over.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not teach (this material) to
All the more so
He pressed (or pressured) him
And he agreed (was won over)

phrases.english: He said to him: We do not teach it
neither to people of Lod nor to people of Neharde'a,
and all the more so you, who are from Lod
and live in Neharde'a.
He pressed him, and he agreed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין נִידּוֹנִין לֹא לְלוּדִּים וְלֹא לִנְהַרְדְּעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן responds based on the background details he asked about in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At first he refuses because of רבי שמלאי's ties to לוד and נהרדעא, but he agrees after being pressed

steps.title: רבי שמלאי asks to learn it in three months
steps.stepSummary: After רבי יוחנן agrees, רבי שמלאי asks to be taught ספר יוחסין in just three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי said to him: Teach it to me in three months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי asks for a very short timeframe to learn ספר יוחסין. This request sets up רבי יוחנן's angry reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had just been persuaded to teach him. Now רבי שמלאי asks to finish the whole thing in three months, which treats a huge body of material as if it were easy.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn it / teach it to me
Three months

phrases.english: He said to him: Let us learn it in three months.
phrases.notes: "It" refers to ספר יוחסין, the Book of Genealogies, from Step 10.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נִיתְנְיֵיהּ בִּתְלָתָא יַרְחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: once רבי יוחנן agrees to teach, רבי שמלאי sets a timeframe.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן will teach ספר יוחסין within three months.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rebukes him using ברוריה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן throws a clod of dirt at him and says that even ברוריה, who learned 300 laws a day, could not finish this material in three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן took a clod of dirt and threw it at him. He said: ברוריה, wife of רבי מאיר and daughter of רבי חנניה בן תרדיון, learned three hundred laws a day from three hundred teachers. Even so, she did not finish her duty in this material in three years. And you say three months?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the request sharply. He uses ברוריה's story to show how unrealistic three months is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a comparison from greater to lesser. ברוריה was brilliant and learned huge amounts every day, yet three years were not enough for her. So three months could never be enough for רבי שמלאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A clod of earth
Threw it at him
ברוריה, wife of רבי מאיר, a famous scholar
Halachic teachings / laws
She did not fulfill her obligation (did not finish properly)

steps.confusionAlert: "Three hundred laws a day" describes ברוריה's general brilliance in learning. It does not mean ספר יוחסין is made of 300 laws. The point is that even someone that fast could not finish this material in three years.

phrases.english: He took a clod of dirt and threw it at him,
he said to him: Now if Beruriah,
the wife of Rabbi Meir,
the daughter of Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon,
who learned three hundred laws in a day
from three hundred teachers,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לֹא יָצְתָה יְדֵי חוֹבָתָהּ
phrases.english: and even so did not fulfill her obligation
in three years,
and you say in three months?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקַל קָלָא פְּתַק בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the three-month request made in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the request to learn ספר יוחסין in three months.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The timeframe is absurdly short. Even ברוריה could not do it in three years.

steps.title: As he leaves, רבי שמלאי asks a halachic question
steps.stepSummary: While leaving, רבי שמלאי asks why mixed intent about the offering's identity disqualifies a פסח, while mixed intent about who eats it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As he was getting up to leave, רבי שמלאי said to him: My teacher, what is the difference between slaughtering a פסח for its own sake and not for its own sake, and slaughtering it for those who can eat it and those who cannot?
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns back to halacha. רבי שמלאי asks about two kinds of mixed intent when slaughtering a פסח, and this question sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha is that mixing לשמו with שלא לשמו disqualifies the פסח. But mixing eaters who are registered with eaters who are not (לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו) leaves it valid. Both are partly wrong intentions, so רבי שמלאי asks why they are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: As he was leaving (literally: taking himself and going)
What is the difference between
For its own sake (as a פסח) and not for its own sake (as another offering)
For those who may eat it and for those who may not

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve mixed intent: part correct and part wrong. The question is not about fully wrong intent. It asks why a half-wrong intent ruins the פסח in one case but not in the other.

phrases.english: As he was leaving, he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי, מָה בֵּין לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: My teacher, what is the difference between for its sake and not for its sake,
and for its eaters and not for its eaters?
phrases.notes: The first case disqualifies the פסח. The second case does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי, מָה בֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the story to a halachic question, connected to the theme of slaughtering a פסח שלא לשמו from earlier in the sugya.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason mixed לשמו and שלא לשמו intent disqualifies a פסח, while mixed intent about eaters does not.

steps.title: First answer: the flaw is in the offering itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that wrong intent about the offering's identity is a flaw in the body of the offering. Wrong intent about the eaters is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Since you are a young Torah scholar, come and I will tell you. For its sake and not for its sake: the disqualification is in the offering itself. For its eaters and not for its eaters: the disqualification is not in the offering itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן is impressed by the question and gives his first answer. He explains the difference by asking where the flaw sits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלא לשמו changes what the offering is, so the flaw is in the animal itself. The wrong eaters are about the people, not the animal, so the offering stays whole and valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A young Torah scholar (literally: one who is 'heated' by the rabbis)
Come and I will tell you
Its disqualification is in its own body (the offering itself)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a flaw in the object itself is more severe than a flaw in something outside it, like the people involved.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוֹאִיל וְצוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן אַתְּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Since you are a young Torah scholar,
come and I will tell you:
For its sake and not for its sake — its disqualification is in itself,

phrases.aramaic: לְאוֹכְלָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו — אֵין פְּסוּלוֹ בְּגוּפוֹ.
phrases.english: for its eaters and not for its eaters — its disqualification is not in itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוֹאִיל וְצוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן אַתְּ, תָּא וְאֵימָא לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to רבי שמלאי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Intent about the offering's identity is a flaw in the offering itself. Intent about the eaters is outside the offering.

steps.title: Second answer: the problem can or cannot be sorted out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a second difference. With mixed identity intent, there is no way to separate the forbidden part. With mixed eaters, the forbidden part can be identified.
steps.simpleTranslation: For its sake and not for its sake: it is impossible to sort out what is forbidden. For its eaters and not for its eaters: it is possible to sort out what is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second, separate reason for the difference. He continues with two more differences in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the intent is both פסח and another offering, the whole animal is mixed, and no part can be called the valid part. If the intent is for both proper and improper eaters, the meat can be divided, so the valid portion goes to the proper eaters. Since the problem can be separated out, the offering stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible to separate or clarify
Its prohibition (the forbidden part)

steps.whatToRemember: So far, two reasons that mixed identity intent disqualifies a פסח but mixed eaters intent does not: (1) the identity flaw is in the offering itself, and (2) the identity flaw cannot be separated out, while the eaters flaw can. רבי יוחנן adds two more differences in steps 17–18.

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ — אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָרֵר אִיסּוּרוֹ,
phrases.english: For its sake and not for its sake — it is impossible to sort out its prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: לְאוֹכְלָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו — אֶפְשָׁר לְבָרֵר אִיסּוּרוֹ.
phrases.english: for its eaters and not for its eaters — it is possible to sort out its prohibition.
phrases.notes: The meat can be divided so the valid eaters get their share.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ — אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָרֵר אִיסּוּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forbidden element in mixed eaters intent can be separated out. In mixed identity intent, it cannot.

steps.title: Third difference: identity-intent works in all four rites
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that wrong intent about the offering's identity (שלא לשמו) can disqualify during all four עבודות. Wrong intent about the eaters (שלא לאוכליו) does not work in all four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Mixed intent of 'for its own purpose and not for its own purpose' applies in all four rites. Mixed intent of 'for its eaters and not for its eaters' does not apply in all four rites.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן is still answering רבי שמלאי's question, and he gives a third difference between the two kinds of wrong intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four main rites of a קרבן are שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה and זריקה. Wrong intent about the offering's identity can ruin the קרבן during any of these four. Wrong intent about the eaters is limited and does not reach all four, so it is a weaker kind of flaw.

keyTerms.meaning: The four core rites of a sacrifice: slaughtering, receiving the blood, carrying it, and sprinkling it
It applies / it exists (in this case)
It does not apply

phrases.english: For its own purpose and not for its own purpose —
applies in all four rites,
for its eaters and not for its eaters —
phrases.notes: Intent that the offering is for people who are signed up to eat it and also for people who are not.

phrases.english: does not apply in all four rites.
phrases.notes: Intent about who will eat it has no effect at the time of sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּאַרְבַּע עֲבוֹדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third distinction to the two given in Steps 15 and 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why identity-intent disqualifies a mixed פסח while eater-intent does not (from Step 14).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Identity-intent has a wider reach, since it works in all four rites. Eater-intent does not.

steps.title: Fourth difference: identity-intent applies to communal offerings too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that identity-intent disqualifies communal offerings (ציבור) just as it does private ones (יחיד). Eater-intent does not apply to communal offerings the way it does to private ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Mixed intent of 'for its own purpose and not for its own purpose' applies to the community just as to an individual. Mixed intent of 'for its eaters and not for its eaters' does not apply to the community as it does to an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his fourth and last difference between the two kinds of wrong intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Identity-intent is a general rule that covers every kind of קרבן, whether it belongs to the whole community or to one person. Eater-intent is not that universal, because it does not work the same way for communal offerings. This again shows that identity-intent is the stronger flaw, so it can ruin a פסח even when it is mixed with correct intent.

keyTerms.meaning: The community, here meaning communal offerings
An individual, here meaning a private person's offering
Just as with an individual

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's four differences all say the same thing: identity-intent is a strong flaw that hits the offering itself, works in all four rites, and applies to every kind of קרבן. Eater-intent is weaker on every count.

phrases.english: For its own purpose and not for its own purpose —
applies to the community as to an individual,
for its eaters and not for its eaters —
does not apply to the community as to an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּצִיבּוּר כִּבְיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's list of four differences.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Identity-intent applies to every type of offering. Eater-intent does not apply equally to communal offerings.

steps.title: רב אשי: two of the reasons are really one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that 'the flaw is in the offering's body' and 'the forbidden part cannot be separated out' are not two separate reasons. The second reason is simply what explains the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'Its disqualification is in its body' and 'it is impossible to separate out its prohibition' are one point. Why did he say its disqualification is in its body? Because it is impossible to separate out its prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי looks back at רבי יוחנן's list and argues that the first two items should be merged into one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15 and 16 seemed to give two separate reasons. רב אשי says the flaw counts as 'in the body' of the offering precisely because you cannot point to any separate forbidden part. So the second reason is the explanation of the first, and the list really has one fewer independent reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It is one and the same thing
What is the reason?
To separate out / identify

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying רבי יוחנן's reasons are wrong. He only says that two of them are one idea seen from two angles.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'Its disqualification is in its body'
and 'it is impossible to separate out its prohibition' —
are one thing,
for what is the reason he said its disqualification is in its body?
Because it is impossible to separate out its prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר פְּסוּלוֹ בְּגוּפוֹ וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָרֵר אִיסּוּרוֹ חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-examines how Steps 15 and 16 should be counted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects counting Step 16 as a reason independent of Step 15.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'cannot separate the prohibition' point is the reason behind the 'flaw in the body' point, so it is not a separate reason.

steps.title: Since ספר יוחסין was hidden, the Sages grew weaker
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר רב יודא quotes רב: from the day ספר יוחסין was hidden away, the Sages' strength weakened and the light of their eyes dimmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר רב יודא said in the name of רב: From the day ספר יוחסין was hidden, the strength of the Sages weakened and the light of their eyes grew dim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the halachic discussion. Since ספר יוחסין was mentioned in the רבי שמלאי story, it brings an aggadic statement about that book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ספר יוחסין was a commentary on דברי הימים that held a great deal of Torah insight. Once it was lost, the Sages lost access to that knowledge. That is why רב describes their strength and vision as dimmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Was hidden away / stored out of use
Their strength weakened
The light of their eyes dimmed

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר רַב יוּדָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rami bar Rav Yuda said that Rav said:
From the day the Book of Genealogies was hidden
the strength of the Sages weakened
and the light of their eyes dimmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר רַב יוּדָא אָמַר רַב מִיּוֹם שֶׁנִּגְנַז סֵפֶר יוּחֲסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up on ספר יוחסין from the רבי שמלאי story (Steps 12–13).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Losing ספר יוחסין weakened the Torah strength and understanding of the Sages.

steps.title: Four hundred camel-loads of teachings between two verses
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says that the expositions on the verses between the two mentions of 'אצל' in דברי הימים would fill four hundred camel-loads.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Between 'אצל' and 'אצל' they loaded four hundred camels' worth of expositions.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא adds another statement showing how huge the lost material of ספר יוחסין was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two nearly identical verses in דברי הימים (א ח:לח and א ט:מד) both list the six sons of אצל. The teachings on just the passage between them were so many that, as an exaggeration, they would take four hundred camels to carry. This explains why רבי יוחנן said the book could not be learned in three months.

keyTerms.meaning: A person named in דברי הימים whose six sons are listed twice
They loaded / carried
Camel-loads of expositions

steps.whatToRemember: The ספר יוחסין stories show how vast this lost Torah was. Even the material between two similar verses was enormous, which is why רבי יוחנן refused to teach it in three months.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
Between 'Azel' and 'Azel'
phrases.notes: Refers to דברי הימים א ח:לח and ט:מד, which have nearly identical wording.

phrases.english: they loaded four hundred camels of expositions.
phrases.notes: An exaggeration that stresses how much material there was.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בֵּין אָצֵל לְאָצַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the praise of ספר יוחסין begun in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The expositions on even a small section of דברי הימים in ספר יוחסין were enormous in number.

steps.title: אחרים say the order of intent matters
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אחרים. For a פסח slaughtered with both מולים and ערלים in mind, it is valid if the מולים were mentioned first and invalid if the ערלים were mentioned first.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say, if he put the circumcised before the uncircumcised, the offering is valid. If he put the uncircumcised before the circumcised, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with a new opinion, from אחרים. It says the order in which the slaughterer thinks of the two groups decides whether the פסח is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a פסח for ערלים, who are not allowed to eat it, disqualifies it. When the slaughterer has both groups in mind, אחרים say it depends on who came first. Mentioning the מולים first keeps the offering valid, while mentioning the ערלים first ruins it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', an unnamed תנא (often identified as רבי מאיר) whose opinion is quoted under this title
He put first, meaning he had this group in mind before the other
Circumcised men, who are allowed to eat the קרבן פסח
Uncircumcised men, who are not allowed to eat the קרבן פסח
Valid / invalid

steps.confusionAlert: 'מולים לערלים' here does not mean 'circumcised people for uncircumcised people'. It means 'circumcised first, then uncircumcised', describing the order in which he thought of them.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Acherim say:
If he put the circumcised before the uncircumcised, it is valid,
but if he put the uncircumcised before the circumcised, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the aggadic statements about ספר יוחסין and דברי הימים. It returns to the laws of intent regarding who will eat the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the intent covers both groups, mentioning the מולים first keeps the פסח valid and mentioning the ערלים first disqualifies it.

steps.title: Why should the order make a difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the offering is valid when the מולים come first because disqualifying it needs all the eaters to be ערלים. It then points out that the same logic should make it valid when the ערלים come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about circumcised before uncircumcised, that it is valid? Because we need the whole group to be uncircumcised, and that is not the case. But when the uncircumcised come before the circumcised too, we need the whole group to be uncircumcised, and that is not the case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אחרים. The reason that explains why the 'מולים first' case is valid seems to apply just as well to the 'ערלים first' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The likely reason for validity is that a פסח is only disqualified if it was slaughtered entirely for ערלים, and a mixed group does not meet that condition. In both orders the group is mixed. So why should putting the ערלים first change anything? The challenge is left hanging for the גמרא to answer next.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Used to demand the difference between two cases that seem the same
We need it to be entirely for ערלים, meaning disqualification requires all the intended eaters to be uncircumcised
And that is not the case here
Also / too

phrases.english: What is different about circumcised before uncircumcised, that it is valid?
Is it because we require it to be entirely for the uncircumcised, and that is not the case?
Then with uncircumcised before circumcised, also,
we require it to be entirely for the uncircumcised, and that is not the case!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מוּלִין לַעֲרֵלִים דְּכָשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction that אחרים drew in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of אחרים that 'ערלים first' disqualifies the פסח while 'מולים first' does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only reasonable explanation for the valid case is that disqualification requires all the eaters to be ערלים. That condition is missing in both orders, so the two cases should have the same ruling.
